$comment: Generated by npm run registry:write from secrets/manifest/*.json. Edit those, not this file.

entries.name: INSTANCE_NAME
entries.description: Display name of the business this instance serves.
howToGet: Use the business's public name.

entries.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
entries.description: Permanent id of the business. Every row in the database is tagged with it.
howToGet: Lowercase the business name and replace spaces with dashes. Never change it after the first deploy.

entries.name: ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS
entries.description: Comma-separated catalog ids of the integrations this instance uses. Secrets for an integration are only required once it is listed here, and each built connector listed syncs on a schedule.
howToGet: Start empty and add each integration as you connect it.

entries.name: SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES
entries.description: Minutes between the end of one sync round and the start of the next, for every connector listed in ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS.
howToGet: Leave empty for 60. Use 5 to 1440.

entries.name: INSTANCE_API_KEY
entries.description: Key that agents and connectors send to call this instance's API.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.

entries.name: WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.description: Signs and verifies webhooks this instance sends or receives.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.

entries.name: SUPABASE_URL
entries.description: Address of this client's own Supabase project.
howToGet: Open supabase.com/dashboard and pick this client's project (each client gets its own).
Go to Project Settings > API.
Copy the Project URL.

entries.name: SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
entries.description: Public (anon or publishable) key for the same Supabase project.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, go to Project Settings > API.
Copy the anon public key (or the publishable key).
It must come from the same project as SUPABASE_URL, or Supabase answers HTTP 401.

entries.name: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
entries.description: Server-only key that bypasses row-level security. Never put it in a browser or app.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, go to Project Settings > API and copy the service_role (or secret) key.

entries.name: SUPABASE_DB_URL
entries.description: Direct Postgres connection string. The instance uses it to store data and run migrations.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, click Connect at the top of the dashboard.
Copy the URI connection string (Session pooler works everywhere).
Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with the database password you set when creating the project.

entries.name: DOC_REGISTRY_IDS
entries.description: Comma-separated ids of the source-of-truth docs reasoning must consult. Optional, but without it every recommendation is marked degraded.
howToGet: Leave as is unless you maintain your own documentation registry.

entries.name: ENABLED_WRITES
entries.description: Comma-separated writes to outside systems this instance allows. Empty keeps every integration read-only.
howToGet: Leave empty. Every integration starts read-only.
Only after the client agrees in writing, list the exact actions, e.g. shopify:adjust_inventory, or shopify:* for every Shopify action.

entries.name: ENABLED_DEPARTMENTS
entries.description: Comma-separated retail departments this instance runs. Empty runs all of them.
howToGet: Leave empty to run every retail department.
To start smaller, list only the ids from docs/departments/README.md that the store uses.

entries.name: RAW_RETENTION_DAYS
entries.description: Days raw vendor data is kept before it is cleared. Facts, signals and links back to the source stay.
howToGet: Leave empty to keep 30 days.
Set a whole number from 1 to 365 if the client's policy asks for a different window.

entries.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: OAuth client for Gmail and Google Drive access.
howToGet: In console.cloud.google.com, create a project, enable the Gmail and Drive APIs, and create an OAuth client ID (Web application).

entries.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Secret for the Google OAuth client.
howToGet: Shown next to the OAuth client ID in Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials.

entries.name: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI
entries.description: Where Google sends the owner back after granting access.
howToGet: Use https://<instance-host>/oauth/google/callback and add it to the OAuth client's authorized redirect URIs.

entries.name: CUSTOMER_REF_KEY
entries.description: Key for customer references: a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256) of a customer's id in a system, email address or phone number, so one customer's records link up across systems without the id or any contact detail being stored. Changing it breaks those links, so it is never rotated.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Keep a copy in the password manager: losing it means a customer's earlier records no longer link to new ones.

entries.name: CORRESPONDENT_HASH_KEY
entries.description: The instance's own key for turning people's identifiers (email addresses, Slack user ids) into private references (HMAC-SHA256), so the brain can tell that two messages or appointments involve the same person without keeping who they are. Without the key, a reference can't be matched against a guessed identifier.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
Don't rotate it unless a leak is suspected: a new key gives every person a new reference, so earlier history no longer lines up with later messages and appointments.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID
entries.description: The directory (tenant) id of the store's Microsoft 365 organization, which each Microsoft app (OneDrive's, Outlook's) signs in to.
howToGet: Signed in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as an admin, open Overview and copy the Tenant ID.

entries.name: AFFIRM_PUBLIC_API_KEY
entries.description: The merchant's Affirm public API key, sent with the private key as HTTP Basic auth to read transactions, disputes and settlements.
howToGet: An Affirm merchant administrator opens API keys in the Affirm merchant portal (www.affirm.com/dashboard/apikeys for a live account, sandbox.affirm.com/dashboard/apikeys for the sandbox one).
Copy the public API key straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: AFFIRM_PRIVATE_API_KEY
entries.description: The merchant's Affirm private API key. Affirm can't limit a key to reading, so this one could also capture, refund and void loans; the connector only ever sends its listed GET reads.
howToGet: On the same API keys page, copy the private API key straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Use the sandbox page's keys with AFFIRM_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox and the live page's keys with production; each environment has its own pair.

entries.name: AFFIRM_MERCHANT_ID
entries.description: The Affirm Merchant ID, which Affirm's settlement reads require. Not a secret, but it names the merchant's account.
howToGet: Ask Affirm merchant support (the Support widget in the merchant portal) for the account's Merchant ID as the settlements API takes it, and copy it here.

entries.name: AFFIRM_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Affirm host the keys are for: sandbox (sandbox.affirm.com) or production (api.affirm.com). There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a live account by accident and the other way round. Canadian accounts on Affirm's global hosts aren't supported yet.
howToGet: Use sandbox with the keys from sandbox.affirm.com/dashboard/apikeys and production with the live keys.

entries.name: AFFIRM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The signing secret Affirm signs webhooks with (Affirm-Signature, HMAC-SHA512). Affirm's docs say it is the merchant's private API key unless Affirm set up another. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Affirm sets webhooks and their signature up itself: ask through the Support widget in the merchant portal, and ask which secret signs them.
Copy that secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: AIRTABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: An Airtable personal access token the connector reads bases, tables and records with. Give it only the data.records:read and schema.bases:read scopes, and access to only the bases to sync. Airtable doesn't report a personal access token's scopes, so the connector can't check them; an OAuth token with any write scope stops the sync.
howToGet: Sign in to Airtable as a user who can see the bases to sync.
Open the builder hub, choose Personal access tokens, then Create token, and name it KaratOS.
Add only the data.records:read and schema.bases:read scopes, and under Access add only the bases to sync.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Airtable shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: AIRTABLE_BASE_IDS
entries.description: The ids of the Airtable bases to read, separated by commas. Unset reads every base the token can see.
howToGet: Open the base in Airtable and copy the part of the address that starts with app, before the next slash.

entries.name: AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The LWA client id of a private Selling Partner API app registered in the seller's own Seller Central account. Not a secret on its own.
howToGet: In Seller Central, open Apps and Services, then Develop Apps, and complete the developer profile if Amazon asks for it.
Add a new app client of type SP-API for private use, with only the Finance and Accounting, and Amazon Fulfillment, roles.
Open the app's LWA credentials and copy the Client identifier.

entries.name: AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The same app's LWA client secret. It goes only to Login with Amazon's token endpoint, in the form body.
howToGet: In the app's LWA credentials, view and copy the Client secret.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Amazon asks for the secret to be rotated every 180 days; add the new one here when it is.

entries.name: AMAZON_SP_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the seller authorizing the app (self-authorization for a private app). The connector trades it for an hour-long access token and only ever sends GETs. It doesn't change when used, and stops working if the seller removes the app.
howToGet: In Develop Apps, open the app's menu and choose Authorize app, then Generate refresh token.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: AMAZON_SP_MARKETPLACE_ID
entries.description: The marketplace to read. ATVPDKIKX0DER (Amazon.com) when unset.
howToGet: Leave unset for Amazon.com, or copy the id of the marketplace from Amazon's marketplace id list.

entries.name: AMAZON_SP_REGION
entries.description: The SP-API region the marketplace belongs to: na (North America, the default), eu (Europe, the Middle East and India) or fe (Japan, Australia and Singapore).
howToGet: Leave unset for a North American marketplace.

entries.name: AMAZON_SP_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: production, or sandbox for Amazon's SP-API sandbox. production when unset.
howToGet: Leave unset unless testing against Amazon's sandbox.

entries.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
entries.description: Lets Brain A use Claude for reasoning.
howToGet: Go to console.anthropic.com > API Keys and create a key named after this instance.

entries.name: ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: An Asana access token the connector reads projects, sections, tasks and comments with. A personal access token can do anything its user can in Asana and can't be limited, so make it as a user who sees only the projects to sync. An OAuth app's token limited to read scopes is the safer choice. The connector only sends its own reads either way.
howToGet: Sign in to Asana as a user who can see the projects to sync and no more, such as a guest or member added only to those projects.
Open the developer console (My apps), choose Create new token under personal access tokens, and name it KaratOS.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Asana shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID
entries.description: The id of the one Asana workspace to read. Unset reads every workspace the token's user belongs to.
howToGet: Open any project in the workspace and ask the client's Asana admin for the workspace id, or open https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/users/me signed in as the token's user and copy the gid of the workspace to read.

entries.name: AURORA_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client ID of a Flute (Aurora Payments) API key made for KaratOS. Flute uses it with the secret to hand out a short-lived token.
howToGet: Signed in to the Flute dashboard, open Merchants, choose the business, then API Keys, and create a key named KaratOS.

Where the business is under a partner, ask the partner to allow the key only List Transactions, Get Transaction Details and Get Settlement Batches. A merchant's own key can reach every endpoint; the connector sends only those reads.
Flute shows the secret once. Copy both straight into the host's secret store. Never paste them into chat or an issue.

entries.name: AURORA_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The client secret of the same Flute API key. It goes only to Flute's OAuth server.
howToGet: Shown once, with the client ID, when the API key is made.

entries.name: AURORA_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Optional. production for the business's own Flute account, or sandbox for a Flute sandbox account. Defaults to production.
howToGet: Leave it unset for the business's own account.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_API_LOGIN_ID
entries.description: The merchant's Authorize.net API Login ID, used with the Transaction Key to read transaction reports.
howToGet: In the Authorize.net Merchant Interface, go to Account > Settings > Security Settings > API Credentials and Keys.
Copy the API Login ID straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_TRANSACTION_KEY
entries.description: The merchant's Authorize.net Transaction Key. Authorize.net can't limit a key to reading, so this one could also charge, refund and void; the connector only ever sends reporting requests.
howToGet: On the same API Credentials and Keys page, create a new Transaction Key. Leave Disable Old Key unticked if another system still uses the current one.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Authorize.net shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Under Account > Settings > Security Settings > Transaction Details API, make sure the Transaction Details API is turned on; the connector reads through it.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Authorize.net endpoint the account is on: sandbox for a developer sandbox account, production for a merchant's live one. There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a live account by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use sandbox with keys from a sandbox account made at developer.authorize.net, and production with the merchant's live keys.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_SIGNATURE_KEY
entries.description: The Signature Key Authorize.net signs webhooks with (X-ANET-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the API Credentials and Keys page, create a new Signature Key and copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: AVALARA_ACCOUNT_ID
entries.description: The AvaTax account number the license key belongs to. Not a secret, but it names the account. The connector checks that AvaTax signs in to this account.
howToGet: In AvaTax, open Settings > License and API Keys and copy the Account ID shown there.

entries.name: AVALARA_LICENSE_KEY
entries.description: The AvaTax license key, sent with the account ID as HTTP Basic credentials. AvaTax can't limit a license key to reading, so it can do anything the account can; the connector only sends its three listed reads whatever the key allows.
howToGet: In AvaTax, an account administrator opens Settings > License and API Keys and, on the License Keys tab, chooses Generate New Keys. Where the account allows several keys, make one for KaratOS alone so it can be revoked on its own; where it allows one, a new key can replace the old, so first check nothing else still uses it.
Copy the key straight into the host's secret store. AvaTax shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: AVALARA_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which AvaTax the account is in: sandbox (sandbox-rest.avatax.com) or production (rest.avatax.com). There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a live account by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use production for the store's live account and sandbox for a developer sandbox account.

entries.name: AVALARA_COMPANY_CODE
entries.description: Optional. The code of the AvaTax company to read. Empty means the account's default company.
howToGet: Leave empty when the account has one company. Otherwise open Settings > Manage companies in AvaTax and copy the Company code of the store's company.

entries.name: BANK_STATEMENTS_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder of statement exports, with one subfolder per account named for its type and last four digits, such as checking-1234 or card-5678. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Inside it, make one folder per account, named like checking-1234, savings-2345 or card-5678.
Download each account's activity as CSV from online banking into its folder.

entries.name: BANK_STATEMENTS_PROFILES
entries.description: Which columns each bank's exports use: generic, or the path to a JSON file in the client's private instance repo mapping account folders to parsing profiles.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the exports have Date, Description and Amount (or Debit and Credit) columns.
Otherwise write the profiles in the client's private instance repo and put the file's path here.

entries.name: EJEWELRY_TENANT_ID
entries.description: The Microsoft Entra tenant id (a GUID) of the jeweler's Business Central, where e-Jewelry runs.
howToGet: The tenant id is the GUID on the Microsoft Entra admin center's overview page for the jeweler's organization, the same tenant the Business Central environment belongs to.

entries.name: EJEWELRY_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: The name of the Business Central environment e-Jewelry runs in, such as production.
howToGet: The environment's name is in the Business Central web address, after the tenant, and in the admin center's list of environments.

entries.name: EJEWELRY_COMPANY_ID
entries.description: The id (a GUID) of the Business Central company that holds the jeweler's e-Jewelry data.
howToGet: Business Central's API lists each company with its id, as the companies reference page shows. Pick the company e-Jewelry's data is in.

entries.name: EJEWELRY_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The application (client) id of the Microsoft Entra app registered for KaratOS, set up in Business Central with read-only permission sets.
howToGet: An administrator registers an app in Microsoft Entra with the Dynamics 365 Business Central application permission and grants admin consent, as Microsoft's service-to-service guide describes. Entra offers no read-only permission for Business Central, so what the app can do is set in the next step.

In Business Central, on the Microsoft Entra Applications page, add the app's client id, set it to Enabled and give it only read-only permission sets that cover items, vendors, and sales and purchase invoices. Never SUPER.
Copy the application (client) id.

entries.name: EJEWELRY_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: A client secret of that Microsoft Entra app. It is sent only to Microsoft's sign-in for a token.
howToGet: Add a client secret to the app in Microsoft Entra, with an end date no more than a year away.
Copy its value straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_STORE_HASH
entries.description: The BigCommerce store's hash, the short ID in its API path (api.bigcommerce.com/stores/<hash>/). Not a secret. The connector checks that the token belongs to this store before reading anything.
howToGet: It is shown as the API path when the store-level API account is created (Settings > Store-level API accounts), between /stores/ and /v3/.
It also appears in the store's control panel address: store-<hash>.mybigcommerce.com.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Access token of a store-level API account holding read-only scopes. BigCommerce can't report a token's scopes, so give it nothing but read-only scopes; the connector also sends only GET requests to its listed paths.
howToGet: In the BigCommerce control panel open Settings > Store-level API accounts > Create API account, type V2/V3 API token, named KaratOS.
Set these scopes to read-only and leave every other scope at None: Orders, Products (which covers price lists), Customers, Information & settings, Store inventory. Never choose modify.
Save, then copy the Access token straight into the host's secret store. BigCommerce shows it once; never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Shared secret BigCommerce sends in the x-karatos-webhook-secret header of each webhook, set as a custom header when the webhook is created, since store webhooks carry no signature. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
Create each webhook (POST /v3/hooks) with headers {"x-karatos-webhook-secret": <this value>}.

entries.name: BILL_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client id of a BILL developer app made with accounting data access. It is sent to BILL only, with the secret, to sign in.
howToGet: Sign in to the BILL web app as a user who can see bills, vendors and payments, and create a developer app there, as BILL's OAuth client credentials guide at developer.bill.com describes.
Name the app for KaratOS and choose Accounting data access, which leaves out payment creation and funding account updates. Never choose Full access.
Copy the client id.

entries.name: BILL_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The developer app's client secret. BILL has no read-only option; with accounting data access it can't create payments or change funding accounts, and the connector only ever reads.
howToGet: Copy the client secret BILL shows when the app is created. It lasts two years; make a new one before then.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: BILL_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: production (the default) reads the business's BILL organization; sandbox uses BILL's sandbox, with a sandbox app's id and secret.
howToGet: Leave unset for the live organization.

entries.name: BIRDEYE_API_KEY
entries.description: The business's Birdeye API key. Birdeye keys carry no scopes, so the same key could reply to reviews; the connector only ever sends Get Reviews. It goes only to Birdeye, in an x-api-key header.
howToGet: In the Birdeye dashboard, find the business's API key (Birdeye support can point to it if it isn't shown).
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: BIRDEYE_BUSINESS_ID
entries.description: The numeric id of the Birdeye business (location) whose reviews are read.
howToGet: Copy the business id from the Birdeye dashboard's business settings, or ask Birdeye support for it.

entries.name: CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: A Calendly personal access token with only the users:read and scheduled_events:read scopes, for the scheduled events and invitees the connector reads. Made by an owner or admin it reads the whole organization's appointments; made by anyone else, only their own.
howToGet: Sign in to Calendly as an owner or admin of the organization, so every team member's appointments are read, and open Integrations & apps > API and webhooks.
Choose Get a token now (or Generate new token), name it KaratOS, and pick only the Users read and Scheduled events read scopes. Leave every write scope, and webhooks, unticked.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Calendly shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: CHASE_IMPORT_MODE
entries.description: How Chase data arrives: CSV exports, PDF statements, or both. The client chooses.
howToGet: Ask the client how they want to send statements.
Use manual_csv for CSV exports, manual_pdf for PDF statements, or manual_csv_and_pdf for both (for example CSV for recent activity and PDFs for older years).

entries.name: CHASE_MANUAL_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder where Chase CSV activity downloads or PDF statements are dropped, one subfolder per account. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo, with one subfolder per account named for its type and last four digits, such as checking-1234 or card-5678.
In Chase online banking, download activity as CSV, or statements as PDF, into each account's folder.

entries.name: CLOVER_MERCHANT_ID
entries.description: The Clover merchant's 13-character ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's business. The connector checks that the token answers for this merchant before it reads anything.
howToGet: In the merchant's Clover dashboard, open Settings > View all settings, then Merchants under About Your Business, and copy the 13-character merchant ID.
It also appears in the dashboard's address, after /merchants/.

entries.name: CLOVER_REGION
entries.description: Which Clover API host the merchant is on: north_america (api.clover.com), europe (api.eu.clover.com), latin_america (api.la.clover.com) or sandbox (apisandbox.dev.clover.com). The connector calls no other host.
howToGet: Use the region the merchant's Clover account was opened in: North America (the US and Canada), Europe or Latin America.
Use sandbox only for a developer test merchant.

entries.name: CLOVER_APP_ID
entries.description: App ID of the KaratOS app in the Clover Developer Dashboard, which is the OAuth client_id for refreshing tokens. With CLOVER_APP_SECRET and CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN, the connector keeps its own expiring tokens current.
howToGet: In the Clover Developer Dashboard, open Your Apps, pick the app, then App Settings, and copy the App ID.

In Requested Permissions, tick only Read merchant, Read orders, Read payments, Read inventory and Read customers. No Write permissions: Clover offers no way to check them later, so this is where read-only starts.

entries.name: CLOVER_APP_SECRET
entries.description: App secret of the Clover app. The connector doesn't send it; it is the key the instance seals its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting the merchant.
howToGet: On the app's App Settings page in the Clover Developer Dashboard, copy the App Secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the merchant and set a new CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the merchant with Clover's v2 OAuth flow. Clover retires it on every refresh, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have the merchant install the KaratOS app, then exchange the authorization code at /oauth/v2/token on the merchant's regional host.
Copy the refresh_token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: CLOVER_API_TOKEN
entries.description: A merchant-specific API token, instead of the app sign-in, for one merchant (Clover documents these for test merchants). It doesn't expire; the connector only ever sends it with GET requests.
howToGet: In the merchant's Clover dashboard, open Settings > View all settings > API tokens and create a token.
Tick only the Read permissions for merchant, orders, payments, inventory and customers.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: CLOVER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_CODE
entries.description: The Clover app's webhook auth code, which Clover sends in X-Clover-Auth with every notification. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In the Clover Developer Dashboard, open the app's App Settings > Webhooks, enter the webhook URL and verify it with the code Clover posts to it.
Copy the Clover Auth Code shown there straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: A Typeform personal access token for the account that owns the forms, used to read their definitions and responses.
howToGet: In Typeform, open Account > Personal tokens and generate a new token for KaratOS.
Give it only the forms:read and responses:read scopes. Typeform can't report a token's scopes, so nothing checks this later; the connector only sends GET requests either way.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_FORM_IDS
entries.description: The Typeform forms to read, by id, separated by commas. Not a secret.
howToGet: A form's id is the last part of its link: in https://example.typeform.com/to/u6nXL7 it is u6nXL7.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_API_HOST
entries.description: Which Typeform host the account keeps its responses on: api.typeform.com, api.eu.typeform.com or api.typeform.eu for the newer EU data center. api.typeform.com when empty; the sync stops with the right host named if it is wrong.
howToGet: Leave empty unless the account is on an EU data center; the first sync says which host to set if it is.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The secret set on a Typeform webhook, which signs each delivery (Typeform-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated by npm run secrets:setup. Set the same value as the secret on each form's webhook in Typeform.

entries.name: FORMS_MAPPING_PROFILE
entries.description: How the forms are built: generic, or the path to a form mapping profile JSON kept in the client's private instance repo.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the forms use the question names in docs/integrations.md.
Otherwise write a profile for the client's forms in their private instance repo and put its path here.

entries.name: DOCUSIGN_INTEGRATION_KEY
entries.description: The integration key (client id) of the KaratOS app in the store's Docusign Apps and Keys page. The app uses JWT Grant, so it needs no secret key or redirect for syncing.
howToGet: Signed in to Docusign as an administrator, open Settings > Apps and Keys and choose Add App and Integration Key. Name it KaratOS.
Copy the Integration Key it shows.

entries.name: DOCUSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY
entries.description: The RSA private key of the KaratOS app's key pair, which signs each JWT Grant sign-in. As Docusign shows it, or base64-encoded on one line. It is never sent anywhere.
howToGet: On the KaratOS app in Settings > Apps and Keys, under Service Integration, choose Generate RSA.
Copy the private key straight into the host's secret store, either as shown or base64-encoded on one line. Docusign shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Leave the app's secret keys and redirect URIs empty, apart from the one redirect the consent step in docs/integrations/docusign.md needs.

entries.name: DOCUSIGN_USER_ID
entries.description: The API user id of the Docusign user the connector signs in as. Make it a user whose permission profile can't send envelopes, and who has shared access to the envelopes of the people who send agreements: Docusign has no read-only scope, so this is what keeps the sign-in from being able to send.
howToGet: In Docusign Settings > Users, add a user for KaratOS with the Viewer permission profile, which can't send envelopes (or a copy of it with sending turned off), and give it shared access to the envelopes of each person who sends agreements.
Open Settings > Users, choose that user, and copy its API Username, a GUID.

entries.name: DOCUSIGN_ACCOUNT_ID
entries.description: The API account id of the Docusign account whose envelopes are read.
howToGet: Open Settings > Apps and Keys and copy the API Account ID shown under My Account Information.

entries.name: DOCUSIGN_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Docusign the account is on: production (the default) or developer, for a free developer account used in testing.
howToGet: Leave unset for a store's own account. Set developer only for a Docusign developer account.

entries.name: DOCUSIGN_CONNECT_HMAC_KEYS
entries.description: The HMAC keys of the store's Docusign Connect configuration, separated by commas, which sign each delivery (X-Docusign-Signature-1 and so on). Only needed once Connect is turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In Docusign Settings > Connect, open Connect Keys and choose Add Secret Key. Docusign shows the key once.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
On the Connect configuration, choose the JSON SIM format, include the envelope summary and recipients, and turn on Include HMAC Signature.

entries.name: DROPBOX_APP_KEY
entries.description: The app key of the store's KaratOS app in the Dropbox App Console, a scoped app with only files.metadata.read and files.content.read turned on.
howToGet: Signed in to Dropbox as the account that holds the folder, open the App Console and create an app with Scoped access and Full Dropbox access, named KaratOS.
In the app's Permissions tab, tick only files.metadata.read and files.content.read (account_info.read is always on), and save.
Copy the App key from the Settings tab.

entries.name: DROPBOX_APP_SECRET
entries.description: The app secret of the KaratOS app, which goes with each token refresh. It also checks the signature on Dropbox webhooks.
howToGet: In the KaratOS app's Settings tab in the App Console, choose Show next to App secret.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: DROPBOX_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the account owner approving the KaratOS app once with offline access. Each sync uses it for a four-hour token asked for read scopes only, and stops if Dropbox reports any other scope.
howToGet: Signed in as the account owner, open https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<app key>&response_type=code&token_access_type=offline&scope=files.metadata.read%20files.content.read and choose Allow. Dropbox shows a code.

Exchange the code once with a POST to https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, the code, and the app key and secret, run on the host. The answer's refresh_token is the value.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: DROPBOX_FOLDER
entries.description: The folder to read, with everything below it, as the Dropbox website shows its path. In a team space that path starts at the team's root, such as /Accounting/Statements.
howToGet: Open the folder on the Dropbox website and copy its path from the breadcrumb, starting with /. Choose a folder that holds only the store's documents, not the whole Dropbox.

entries.name: DROPBOX_FILE_NAMES
entries.description: keep (the default) keeps file and folder names, which can name customers; drop keeps only ids, kinds and times.
howToGet: Leave unset to keep names. Set drop if the store names files after customers and would rather not keep them.

entries.name: EBAY_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The App ID (client id) of an eBay developer app the store owns, from its production keyset, or its sandbox keyset when EBAY_ENVIRONMENT is sandbox. Not a secret on its own.
howToGet: Sign in to developer.ebay.com with the store's own developer account and open Application Keys.
Create a keyset for production (and one for the sandbox to test with) and copy its App ID (Client ID).

entries.name: EBAY_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The Cert ID (client secret) of the same keyset. It goes only to eBay's token endpoint, in a Basic header.
howToGet: In Application Keys, copy the keyset's Cert ID (Client Secret).
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: EBAY_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the store's eBay seller account agreeing to the app with only the scope https://api.ebay.com/oauth/api_scope/sell.fulfillment.readonly. Brain A asks for every access token with that scope alone, so eBay turns down any change. It lasts 18 months, then the seller connects again.
howToGet: In User Tokens on developer.ebay.com, add an eBay redirect URL (RuName) for the keyset if it has none.
Choose Get a Token from eBay via Your Application, tick only sell.fulfillment.readonly under OAuth scopes, and sign in as the store's seller account to agree.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Set a reminder to connect again before the 18 months are up.

entries.name: EBAY_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: production (the default) or sandbox, which eBay the keys and token belong to. Not a secret.
howToGet: Leave it unset for the store's real eBay account. Set it to sandbox to test with sandbox keys and a sandbox test user.

entries.name: EDI_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder where the business's VAN or SFTP mailbox keeps its X12 files, both what partners sent and copies of what was sent to them. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Have the VAN or SFTP client copy every inbound and outbound X12 file (.edi, .x12, .txt or .dat) into it. Leave the mailbox itself as it is: KaratOS reads copies and never sends.

entries.name: ETSY_KEYSTRING
entries.description: The keystring of the KaratOS app on Etsy's developer site. It is also the OAuth client id, and goes with the shared secret in every request's x-api-key header.
howToGet: On Etsy's developer site, open Your Apps, then the KaratOS app, and copy its keystring straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: ETSY_SHARED_SECRET
entries.description: The KaratOS app's shared secret on Etsy. Sent only to Etsy, in the x-api-key header. With the keystring, it also encrypts the stored refresh token.
howToGet: On the same Your Apps page, copy the shared secret straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: ETSY_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the shop with transactions_r and listings_r only. It seeds the stored token; the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database. It lasts 90 days without use.
howToGet: Have the shop owner connect the KaratOS app at https://www.etsy.com/oauth/connect with scope "transactions_r listings_r" and nothing else (PKCE is required).
Exchange the code at https://api.etsy.com/v3/public/oauth/token and copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: ETSY_SHOP_ID
entries.description: The numeric id of the Etsy shop to read. The connector stops if the connection belongs to another shop.
howToGet: After connecting, GET https://api.etsy.com/v3/application/users/me answers the shop_id, or copy it from the shop's Etsy settings.

entries.name: FEDEX_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The API key of a FedEx Developer Portal project with the Track API. FedEx calls it the client id; it is sent to FedEx only, with the secret, to sign in.
howToGet: Sign in at developer.fedex.com with the business's FedEx account and create a project for KaratOS.
Choose only the Track API, link the shipping account, and copy the production API key.

entries.name: FEDEX_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The project's secret key. With only the Track API chosen, it can read tracking and nothing else: no labels, pickups or billing.
howToGet: On the same project's page at developer.fedex.com, copy the production secret key.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: FEDEX_TRACKING_NUMBERS_FILE
entries.description: A text or CSV file of the FedEx tracking numbers to follow, one or more a line, such as the labels printed for repairs, memo goods and customer orders. Lines starting with # are skipped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Export the tracking numbers from FedEx Ship Manager's history, the POS or the shipping app.
Save it outside any git repo and put its path here. Add new numbers as parcels go out; delivered ones are no longer read.

entries.name: FEDEX_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: production (the default) reads live tracking; test uses FedEx's sandbox, which only answers its own test numbers.
howToGet: Leave unset for live tracking.

entries.name: FEDEX_MAX_TRACKING_PER_SYNC
entries.description: The most tracking numbers one sync reads, oldest first. Defaults to 500, so a long list stays well inside FedEx's daily call limit.
howToGet: Leave unset for 500.

entries.name: FINCEN_8300_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder holding the store's Form 8300 filings log as CSV, one row per filing. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Start the log from the template in docs/integrations/fincen_8300.md, as a spreadsheet saved as CSV.
After each filing in BSA E-Filing, add a row with the filing date, the sales, the cash, the date it was received and the BSA Tracking ID, then add the BSA ID and status once FinCEN acknowledges it.
Never put names, addresses or taxpayer numbers in the log.

entries.name: FINCEN_8300_DATE_ORDER
entries.description: How the log writes dates: mdy (10/30/2026), dmy (30/10/2026) or ymd (2026-10-30).
howToGet: Leave unset for US dates, month first.

entries.name: GIA_API_URL
entries.description: The Report Results API address GIA gives when the API key is issued. Only https addresses on a gia.edu host are accepted, so the key can't be sent anywhere else.
howToGet: In the GIA Client Portal, apply for Report Results API access under Useful links.
Copy the API address from the signup confirmation.

entries.name: GIA_API_KEY
entries.description: A GIA Report Results API key. It reads reports only. Each plan can have several keys; give KaratOS its own so it can be revoked alone.
howToGet: In the GIA Client Portal, open GET API KEYS and create a key for KaratOS.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: GIA_REPORT_NUMBERS_FILE
entries.description: A text or CSV file of the GIA report numbers to look up, one per line in the first column, such as the certificate numbers on the business's stones. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Export the certificate number column for GIA-graded stones from the POS or inventory system.
Save it outside any git repo and put its path here. Add new numbers to the end; each is looked up once.

entries.name: GIA_MAX_LOOKUPS_PER_SYNC
entries.description: The most new report numbers one sync looks up. Lookups of reports the business didn't submit cost money on a pay-as-you-go plan, so this caps what one sync can spend. Defaults to 100.
howToGet: Leave unset for 100.
Raise it for the first import of a large inventory, after checking the plan's remaining lookups.

entries.name: GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the mailbox with the gmail.metadata scope. Google doesn't rotate it, so this value keeps working until the owner revokes access, changes their password, leaves it unused for six months, or (for an External consent screen still in Testing) seven days pass. The instance keeps a sealed copy in its database in case Google ever returns a new one; replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over.
howToGet: Have the mailbox owner connect the mailbox to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and exactly the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata, for example through Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground using the client's own credentials (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).
The connector stops if the token holds any other Gmail scope (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.labels, gmail.send, gmail.compose or https://mail.google.com/), so don't add them.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GMAIL_USER
entries.description: Which mailbox to read: me (the account that connected, the default) or that account's address. One mailbox per instance. Not a secret, but it names the mailbox.
howToGet: Leave empty for me. Each further mailbox needs its own instance.

entries.name: GMAIL_LABEL_NAMES
entries.description: Whether user label names are kept: keep (the default) keeps names such as Bridal or Vendors, leaving out any with an @ or four digits in a row; drop keeps label ids only, for a mailbox whose labels are named after customers.
howToGet: Leave empty for keep. Use drop if labels in the mailbox carry customers' names.

entries.name: GOOGLE_ADS_CUSTOMER_ID
entries.description: The 10-digit customer id of the Google Ads account Brain A reads. Not a secret.
howToGet: In Google Ads, the customer id is at the top of the page next to the account name, as 123-456-7890. Dashes are fine.

entries.name: GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN
entries.description: The developer token Google Ads issues to a manager account for API access. A new token reads test accounts only; reading the store's real account needs Basic access, which Google grants on application.
howToGet: Sign in to a Google Ads manager account (create one if the store has none) and open Admin > API Center.
Accept the terms and copy the developer token. Apply for Basic access there so it can read a production account.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID
entries.description: The 10-digit customer id of the manager account the connected user reaches the store's account through. Leave it unset when the user signs in to the store's account directly.
howToGet: In the manager account, copy its customer id from the top of the page.

entries.name: GOOGLE_ADS_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting a Google account with access to the Google Ads account, with the adwords scope only. Google Ads has no read-only scope, so give that user Read only access in Google Ads; Brain A only ever sends searches. It is a separate connection from the other Google connectors, because each one stops if its token holds any scope beyond its own.
howToGet: Turn on the Google Ads API in the Google Cloud project that owns the OAuth client.
In Google Ads, open Admin > Access and security and add a Google account with Read only access (a user made for Brain A is best).

Have that account connect to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and only the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords. Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the client's own credentials works (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).
The connector stops if the token holds any other scope, so don't add one.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID
entries.description: The numeric id of the GA4 property Brain A reads reports from. Not a secret, and not the G- measurement id.
howToGet: In Google Analytics, open Admin > Property details and copy the Property ID (digits only).

entries.name: GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting a Google account with Viewer access to the property, with the analytics.readonly scope only. It uses the same OAuth client as Gmail and Google Workspace but is a separate connection, because each connector stops if its token holds any scope beyond its own. Google doesn't rotate it; the instance keeps a sealed copy in case Google ever returns a new one.
howToGet: Turn on the Google Analytics Data API in the Google Cloud project that owns the OAuth client.

Have someone with Viewer access to the property connect to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and only the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly. Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the client's own credentials works (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).
The connector stops if the token holds anything else, such as analytics (which can change settings), analytics.edit or a Drive or Gmail scope, so don't add them.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_ROOT_FOLDER_ID
entries.description: The Drive folder the business shares with Brain A. Everything below it is read as metadata (names, types, folders, sizes, edit times); file contents are never downloaded.
howToGet: Open the folder in Google Drive and copy the id after /folders/ in the address bar.
The Google account that connects must be able to open the folder. A whole shared drive can be read instead, or as well, with GOOGLE_DRIVE_SHARED_DRIVE_IDS.

entries.name: GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the business's Google account with the three read-only scopes drive.metadata.readonly, spreadsheets.readonly and calendar.events.readonly. It uses the same OAuth client as Gmail but is a separate connection, because each connector stops if its token holds any scope beyond its own. Google doesn't rotate it; the instance keeps a sealed copy in case Google ever returns a new one.
howToGet: Have the account owner connect to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and exactly these scopes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.metadata.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly (spreadsheets.readonly only if GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGES is set, calendar.events.readonly only if calendars are read). Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the client's own credentials works (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).

The connector stops if the token holds anything else, such as drive.readonly (which can download files), drive, drive.file, spreadsheets, calendar, calendar.readonly, calendar.events or a Gmail scope, so don't add them.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_SHARED_DRIVE_IDS
entries.description: Shared drives to read whole, besides the shared folder: comma-separated shared drive ids. Each is walked like a folder and gets its own change feed.
howToGet: Leave empty to read only the shared folder.
Open the shared drive in Google Drive and copy the id after /folders/ in the address bar.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_FILE_NAMES
entries.description: Whether file and folder names are kept: keep (the default) or drop, for a business whose files are named after customers. With drop, only ids, types, folders, sizes and times are kept.
howToGet: Leave empty for keep. Use drop if file names carry customers' names.

entries.name: GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGES
entries.description: The only spreadsheet ranges whose values are read: comma-separated spreadsheetId/Sheet!A1:F500 entries. Sheet names may hold letters, digits, spaces, _ . and -, quoted when they hold a space. Nothing else is read from any spreadsheet. List ranges without customers' personal details; a cell that is only an email address is kept as a correspondent reference.
howToGet: Leave empty to read no spreadsheet values.
Open the spreadsheet and copy the id between /d/ and /edit in the address bar, then add / and the range in A1 notation, as Google Sheets shows it.

entries.name: GOOGLE_CALENDAR_IDS
entries.description: Which calendars' appointments are read: primary (the default, the connected account's own calendar), none, or comma-separated calendar ids such as a shared appointments calendar's address. Not a secret, but it names the calendars.
howToGet: Leave empty for primary. Use none to read no calendars.
For another calendar, open its settings in Google Calendar and copy the Calendar ID under Integrate calendar.

entries.name: GOOGLE_PUSH_CHANNEL_TOKEN
entries.description: The token Drive and Calendar push channels are opened with and echo back in X-Goog-Channel-Token, which is how the instance tells a genuine notification from a forged one (Google doesn't sign them). Only used once push channels are turned on through the write gate.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
After rotating it, open new push channels: notifications on the old ones are refused.

entries.name: GORGIAS_DOMAIN
entries.description: The store's Gorgias subdomain: store for store.gorgias.com. Every request goes to that address.
howToGet: Read it from the address bar of the store's Gorgias helpdesk: the part before .gorgias.com.

entries.name: GORGIAS_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client id of the KaratOS app in Gorgias's partner portal, which asks only for openid, offline and tickets:read.
howToGet: In the KaratOS app's settings in Gorgias's partner portal, copy its client id. The app asks for openid, offline and tickets:read and nothing that writes.

entries.name: GORGIAS_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The KaratOS app's client secret, sent only to the store's Gorgias sign-in, with the refresh token, for a one-day token.
howToGet: Copy the client secret from the KaratOS app's settings in Gorgias's partner portal straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GORGIAS_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the store connecting the KaratOS app to its helpdesk. It doesn't expire, and stops working if the store deactivates the app.
howToGet: A Gorgias admin connects the KaratOS app to the store's helpdesk and approves openid, offline and tickets:read.
The connection's callback exchanges the code for tokens; put the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
To revoke it, deactivate the app in the helpdesk's settings.

entries.name: GUSTO_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS app in Gusto's developer portal, used with the client secret to refresh Gusto access tokens.
howToGet: On dev.gusto.com, open the KaratOS application and its OAuth settings.
Copy the Client ID straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: GUSTO_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the Gusto app. It refreshes access tokens and is the key the instance encrypts its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting Gusto.
howToGet: On the application's page in the Gusto developer portal, copy the secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the company and set a new GUSTO_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: GUSTO_REDIRECT_URI
entries.description: The redirect URI registered for the Gusto app. Gusto asks for it on every token refresh. Not a secret.
howToGet: Copy the redirect URI exactly as it is registered on the application's page in the Gusto developer portal.

entries.name: GUSTO_COMPANY_UUID
entries.description: The company's UUID in Gusto. Not a secret, but it names the client's payroll. The connector stops if the token belongs to another company.
howToGet: After the company is connected, call GET /v1/token_info with the access token and copy resource.uuid (resource.type is Company).

entries.name: GUSTO_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the company. Gusto replaces it on every refresh, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Give the KaratOS app only the payrolls:read scope in the Gusto developer portal, then have a company admin connect the company.
The connector rejects a connection holding any scope beyond reading, so don't add others.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GUSTO_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Gusto host to read: production (api.gusto.com) or demo (api.gusto-demo.com). production when empty.
howToGet: Leave empty for a live company. Set demo only for a company in Gusto's demo environment.

entries.name: GUSTO_WEBHOOK_VERIFICATION_TOKEN
entries.description: The verification_token of the Gusto webhook subscription, which signs each delivery (X-Gusto-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: When the webhook subscription is created, Gusto sends the verification_token to its URL. Copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: HRD_API_TOKEN
entries.description: A MyHRD API token. The public MyHRD API only reads report data and report validity, so the token can do nothing else.
howToGet: Sign in to MyHRD at my.hrdantwerp.com and open API Access in the page footer.
Fill in the request form; HRD checks it and emails the token within one to three working days.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: HRD_REPORT_NUMBERS_FILE
entries.description: A text or CSV file of the HRD report numbers to look up, one per line in the first column, such as the report numbers on the business's stones and jewels. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Export the report number column for HRD-graded stones and jewels from the POS or inventory system.
Save it outside any git repo and put its path here. Add new numbers to the end; each is looked up once.

entries.name: HRD_MAX_LOOKUPS_PER_SYNC
entries.description: The most report numbers one sync looks up. HRD allows 1000 lookups a day and 100 requests in 15 minutes, so the rest wait for the next sync. Defaults to 50.
howToGet: Leave unset for 50.
Keep it under 100, HRD's limit for 15 minutes.

entries.name: HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Access token of the HubSpot private app the connector reads contacts, companies, deals, tickets and engagements with. The connector asks HubSpot which scopes it holds before every sync and refuses one that could change data.
howToGet: A HubSpot super admin opens Settings > Integrations > Private Apps (Development > Legacy apps in newer accounts) and creates a private app named KaratOS.

On its Scopes tab, select exactly these read scopes: crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.objects.companies.read, crm.objects.deals.read and crm.objects.tickets.read. Contacts read also covers calls, emails, meetings, notes and tasks.
Don't add any write scope or the older tickets scope, which can change tickets: the connector refuses a token that holds one.
Create the app and copy its access token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: HUBSPOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the HubSpot private app, which signs its webhook deliveries (X-HubSpot-Signature-v3). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the private app's Auth tab in HubSpot, copy the Client secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: IDEX_API_KEY
entries.description: The API key IDEX issues for the Onsite feed. It names the account and isn't secret on its own.
howToGet: Ask the IDEX account manager to turn on the Onsite feed add-on for the trading subscription.
Set the feed's filters and markups on IDEX, then copy the API key IDEX issues for it.

entries.name: IDEX_API_SECRET
entries.description: The API secret that comes with that key. KaratOS sends it only to IDEX's Onsite feed addresses.
howToGet: Copy the API secret IDEX issues with the key.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: IDEX_FEEDS
entries.description: Which Onsite feeds to read: natural, lab_grown, or both comma-separated. Defaults to natural; the lab-grown feed is a separate IDEX add-on.
howToGet: Leave unset for the natural feed only.
Add lab_grown once IDEX has turned on the lab-grown add-on.

entries.name: IDEX_MAX_STONES
entries.description: The most stones one feed may hold before the sync stops and asks for narrower filters on IDEX. Defaults to 50000.
howToGet: Leave unset for 50000.
Raise it only if the feed's filters on IDEX are meant to cover more stones.

entries.name: POS_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder on the owner's machine or the instance's volume where point-of-sale CSV exports are dropped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Export items, stock on hand, customers and sales from the POS as CSV into it. Each export can be a new file; a file that changes is read again.

entries.name: POS_MAPPING_PROFILE
entries.description: Which columns the POS exports use: generic, or the path to a mapping profile JSON kept in the client's private instance repo.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the exports use the column names in docs/integrations.md.
Otherwise write a profile for the client's POS in their private instance repo and put its path here.

entries.name: JUDGEME_SHOP_DOMAIN
entries.description: The shop's domain in Judge.me, such as example.myshopify.com.
howToGet: In Judge.me, open Settings > Integrations and select View API tokens; the shop domain is shown beside the tokens.

entries.name: JUDGEME_API_TOKEN
entries.description: A Judge.me token for reading the shop's reviews: best an OAuth token granted only read_reviews, otherwise the private API token, which can also post and hide reviews. The connector only ever lists reviews. It goes only to Judge.me.
howToGet: Preferred: register a Judge.me OAuth app, ask the shop for the read_reviews scope only, and use the access token it returns.
Otherwise: in Settings > Integrations > View API tokens, copy the private API token. Judge.me can't regenerate it from the admin, so it is replaced through Judge.me support.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: KLAVIYO_PRIVATE_API_KEY
entries.description: A Klaviyo private API key with read-only scopes, for profiles, lists, segments, campaigns, flows and their figures. Klaviyo can't be asked which scopes a key holds, so the connector can't check it; it only sends its listed reads whatever the key allows.
howToGet: In Klaviyo, open Settings > Account > API keys (an Owner, Admin or Manager can) and choose Create Private API Key. Name it KaratOS.

Choose Custom Key and give Read Access to Profiles, Lists, Segments, Campaigns, Flows and Metrics, and No Access to everything else. Never pick Full Access Key, and never reuse an old key: keys made before scopes existed have full access.
Copy the key (pk_...) straight into the host's secret store. Klaviyo shows it once.

entries.name: KLAVIYO_CONVERSION_METRIC_ID
entries.description: Optional. The id of the metric the campaign and flow reports count conversions and revenue by. Empty means the metric named Placed Order, which Klaviyo's own reports use.
howToGet: Leave empty unless the store records orders under another metric. To find one, open Analytics > Metrics in Klaviyo, open the metric and copy the id from the page address.

entries.name: KLAVIYO_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Secret of a Klaviyo system webhook, which signs each delivery (Klaviyo-Signature over the body and Klaviyo-Timestamp). Only Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners can create webhooks; the scheduled sync works without them.
howToGet: Only if the account has webhooks: create the webhook with the Webhooks API, choosing your own random secret_key, and put the same value in the host's secret store.

entries.name: LIGHTSPEED_DOMAIN_PREFIX
entries.description: The store's Lightspeed Retail (X-Series) domain prefix, the part before .retail.lightspeed.app. Not a secret, but it names the client's store.
howToGet: Sign in to the store's Lightspeed Retail and copy the first part of its address: for https://examplestore.retail.lightspeed.app it is examplestore.
This is X-Series (formerly Vend). An R-Series store signs in at a different address and is not supported yet.

entries.name: LIGHTSPEED_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS app on Lightspeed's X-Series developer portal, used with the client secret to refresh access tokens.
howToGet: On Lightspeed's X-Series developer portal, open the KaratOS app and copy its client ID straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: LIGHTSPEED_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the Lightspeed app. It refreshes access tokens and is the key the instance encrypts its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting the store.
howToGet: On the app's page on the developer portal, copy the client secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the store and set a new LIGHTSPEED_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: LIGHTSPEED_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the store. Lightspeed gives a new one on every refresh, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have the store's account owner connect the store to the KaratOS app at https://secure.retail.lightspeed.app/connect with exactly these scopes: products:read inventory:read customers:read sales:read.
The connector stops on a connection holding any scope beyond reading, so don't add others.
Copy the refresh token from the token response straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: MAILCHIMP_API_KEY
entries.description: A Mailchimp API key for the store's account, ending in its data center (for example -us21). Mailchimp keys can't be limited to reading, so the connector sends only its five listed GET reads.
howToGet: Sign in to Mailchimp as an account owner or admin, open Profile > Extras > API keys, and choose Create A Key. Name it KaratOS.
Copy the key straight into the host's secret store. Mailchimp shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
To cut KaratOS off, delete the key on the same page.

entries.name: MAILCHIMP_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: A random secret the instance adds to its Mailchimp webhook URL as ?key=, since Mailchimp doesn't sign deliveries. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Let npm run secrets:setup generate it, or make 32 random bytes as hex.
Register the webhook in the audience's Settings > Webhooks with the instance's URL ending in ?key= and this value.

entries.name: META_APP_ID
entries.description: Meta app for Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp.
howToGet: At developers.facebook.com, create a Business app and copy its App ID.

entries.name: META_APP_SECRET
entries.description: Secret for the Meta app.
howToGet: In the Meta app, go to Settings > Basic and copy the App Secret.

entries.name: WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: System-user token for the WhatsApp Business API.
howToGet: In Meta Business Settings, create a system user, assign the WhatsApp app, and generate a permanent token.

entries.name: WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID
entries.description: The WhatsApp business phone number's id (not the number itself).
howToGet: In the Meta app, go to WhatsApp > API Setup and copy the Phone number ID.

entries.name: META_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: A system user access token from the store's Meta Business account, holding the ads_read permission only, with the ad account assigned to the system user. The connector stops if the token holds anything more, such as ads_management or business_management. A system user token doesn't expire unless it is revoked.
howToGet: In Meta Business Settings, open Users > System users and add a system user with the Employee role (a user made for Brain A is best).
Assign the store's ad account to it with View performance access only.
Choose Generate new token, pick an app the business owns, and tick only ads_read.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: META_ADS_ACCOUNT_ID
entries.description: The numeric id of the ad account Brain A reads, with or without act_. Not a secret.
howToGet: In Meta Ads Manager, the ad account id is in the account menu at the top left, or in Business Settings > Accounts > Ad accounts.

entries.name: METALS_API_KEY
entries.description: Access key for Metals-API spot prices. It can only read prices; Metals-API has nothing to write to.
howToGet: Sign up at metals-api.com. The free plan is enough to start; a paid plan updates more often and allows more requests a month.
Copy the API key from the dashboard.

entries.name: METALS_API_HISTORY_DAYS
entries.description: Days of daily closing prices the first import reads, from 1 to 1825. Every 30 days costs four requests, one per metal.
howToGet: Leave empty for a year (52 requests). Check the plan's monthly request allowance before asking for more.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The application (client) id of the store's KaratOS app registration, given Sites.Selected with the read role on one SharePoint site and nothing else.
howToGet: In the Entra admin center, open App registrations, choose New registration, name it KaratOS, keep single tenant and register it.
In its API permissions, remove User.Read, add the Microsoft Graph application permission Sites.Selected, and grant admin consent. Add nothing else.
Grant the app the read role on the one site that holds the library, as the connector's docs page shows, then copy the Application (client) ID from Overview.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: A client secret of the KaratOS app, sent only to Microsoft's sign-in for a one-hour Graph token. The connector stops if that token carries any permission that isn't a read one.
howToGet: In the KaratOS app's Certificates & secrets, choose New client secret, describe it as KaratOS and pick the shortest expiry the store is happy to renew.
Copy its Value (not its Secret ID) straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_ONEDRIVE_DRIVE_ID
entries.description: The drive id of the document library to read, such as the site's Documents library. It starts with b!.
howToGet: In Graph Explorer, signed in as an admin, run GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{host}:/sites/{site}?$select=id with the site's host and name from its address, and note the id.
Run GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{site id}/drives?$select=id,name and copy the id of the library to read.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_ONEDRIVE_FILE_NAMES
entries.description: keep (the default) keeps file and folder names, which can name customers; drop keeps only ids, kinds and times.
howToGet: Leave unset to keep names. Set drop if the store names files after customers and would rather not keep them.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_GRAPH_CLIENT_STATE
entries.description: The clientState the drive's change notification subscription was made with. Graph sends it back with each notification, and one that carries it prompts the incremental sync.
howToGet: Leave unset to sync on a schedule only, which is what most stores want: Graph only lets an app subscribe to a drive with Files.Read.All, which reads every site and OneDrive in the organization, not Sites.Selected.

To have changes prompt a sync, generate 32 random characters on the host, save them straight into the host's secret store, and use them as clientState when an admin makes the subscription. Never paste them into chat or an issue.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_OUTLOOK_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The application (client) id of the store's KaratOS Outlook app registration. It holds no Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra; Exchange gives it Application Mail.ReadBasic and Application Calendars.Read for the one mailbox through RBAC for Applications.
howToGet: In the Entra admin center, open App registrations, choose New registration, name it KaratOS Outlook, keep single tenant and register it. Remove User.Read from its API permissions and add nothing.
In Exchange Online PowerShell, as an admin, point Exchange at the app with New-ServicePrincipal, using the IDs from the app's Enterprise applications page.

Assign the roles Application Mail.ReadBasic and Application Calendars.Read with New-ManagementRoleAssignment, scoped to the one mailbox through a management scope or an administrative unit, and check with Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization that only that mailbox is in scope.
Copy the Application (client) ID from the app's Overview.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_OUTLOOK_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: A client secret of the KaratOS Outlook app, sent only to Microsoft's sign-in for a one-hour Graph token. The connector stops if that token carries any permission that isn't a read one.
howToGet: In the KaratOS Outlook app's Certificates & secrets, choose New client secret, describe it as KaratOS and pick the shortest expiry the store is happy to renew.
Copy its Value (not its Secret ID) straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_OUTLOOK_MAILBOX
entries.description: The address (or object id) of the one Exchange Online mailbox to read, such as the store's shared sales mailbox.
howToGet: Use the address of the mailbox the role assignments are scoped to. It must be the same one, or Graph answers 403.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_TEAMS_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The application (client) id of the store's KaratOS Teams app registration. It holds no Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra; the team grants it ChannelMessage.Read.Group and ChannelSettings.Read.Group when it installs the app.
howToGet: In the Entra admin center, open App registrations, choose New registration, name it KaratOS Teams, keep single tenant and register it. Remove User.Read from its API permissions and add nothing.

Make a Teams app package whose manifest names this client id under webApplicationInfo and asks, under authorization.permissions.resourceSpecific, for ChannelMessage.Read.Group and ChannelSettings.Read.Group as Application permissions, and nothing else.
Upload it as a custom app in the Teams admin center, allow it, and have an owner of the one team install it there, consenting to those two permissions for that team.
Copy the Application (client) ID from the app's Overview.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_TEAMS_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: A client secret of the KaratOS Teams app, sent only to Microsoft's sign-in for a one-hour Graph token. The connector stops if that token carries any permission that isn't a read one.
howToGet: In the KaratOS Teams app's Certificates & secrets, choose New client secret, describe it as KaratOS and pick the shortest expiry the store is happy to renew.
Copy its Value (not its Secret ID) straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAM_ID
entries.description: The group id of the one team to read, the team the KaratOS Teams app is installed in.
howToGet: In Teams, open the team's menu, choose Get link to team, and copy the groupId value from the link. It must be the team the app is installed in, or Graph answers 403.

entries.name: MONDAY_API_TOKEN
entries.description: monday.com API token the connector reads boards, items and updates with. A monday app's OAuth token granted only boards:read and updates:read is the safer choice, since monday.com then refuses every change. A personal API token carries everything its user can do and can't be limited; the connector still only sends its own read queries.
howToGet: Safer: in monday.com's Developer Center, create an app, give its OAuth settings only the boards:read and updates:read scopes, install it on the account and copy the access token from the OAuth flow. Set MONDAY_OAUTH_SCOPES to the scopes it was granted.
Simpler: as a user who can see the boards to sync, click your avatar > Developers > API token and copy it. It can change anything that user can, so use one with no more access than needed.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: MONDAY_OAUTH_SCOPES
entries.description: For a monday app's OAuth token, the scopes it was granted, as the token response's scope field lists them. The connector refuses to run if any of them could change data. Leave it unset for a personal API token.
howToGet: Copy the scope field from the response that gave the OAuth access token. It should read boards:read updates:read.

entries.name: MONDAY_ALLOWED_COLUMNS
entries.description: Columns whose display text the connector may keep although their type can hold personal data (text, long text, email, phone, location, files, links), as comma-separated board:column pairs. Unset keeps none of them; status, date, numbers, checkbox, dropdown, timeline and people columns are always kept.
howToGet: Only allow a column the business agrees to share, such as a ring size or an order number kept in a text column, never one with customer names or contact details.
The board id is the number in the board's address; the column id shows under the column's menu when Developer mode is on in monday.com's monday labs.

entries.name: MONDAY_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.description: The monday app's Signing Secret, which signs the JWT on webhook deliveries for webhooks the app creates. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In monday.com's Developer Center, open the app, then Basic Information, and copy the Signing Secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: NETSUITE_ACCOUNT_ID
entries.description: The NetSuite account id, as NetSuite writes it: digits, with _SB1 or the like for a sandbox.
howToGet: The account id is the first part of the account's SuiteTalk host, such as 1234567 in 1234567.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com, as NetSuite's SuiteQL guide shows. A sandbox host writes _SB1 as -sb1.

entries.name: NETSUITE_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client id of the integration record made for KaratOS, with the client credentials (machine-to-machine) grant and only the REST web services scope.
howToGet: An administrator creates an integration record with the client credentials (machine-to-machine) grant and only the REST web services scope, as NetSuite's OAuth 2.0 client credentials guide describes.
Copy the client id it shows. The client secret isn't needed.

entries.name: NETSUITE_CERTIFICATE_ID
entries.description: The certificate id NetSuite gives when the administrator maps KaratOS's certificate to the integration record, a role that can only view, and an entity.
