howToGet: Make a role that can only view: items, vendors, the transactions read (sales orders, purchase orders, invoices, journal entries), and locations, with the REST Web Services and Log in using OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens permissions, and nothing that creates or edits.
An administrator maps the certificate to the integration record, that role and an entity, as NetSuite's client credentials guide describes, and copies the certificate id NetSuite gives.

entries.name: NETSUITE_PRIVATE_KEY
entries.description: The private key of the certificate mapped for KaratOS: RSA of 3072 or 4096 bits, or EC on P-256, P-384 or P-521. It signs each sign-in and is never sent anywhere. As PEM, or base64-encoded on one line.
howToGet: Make a key pair and a certificate for it, valid for at most two years, and give the administrator only the certificate to map.
Copy the private key straight into the host's secret store, as PEM or base64-encoded on one line. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: NIVODA_USERNAME
entries.description: The username of the Nivoda account's API access. It names the account and isn't secret on its own.
howToGet: Ask Nivoda to turn on API access for the business's buyer account, starting on staging.
Use the API username Nivoda gives for it.

entries.name: NIVODA_PASSWORD
entries.description: The password that goes with that username. KaratOS sends it only to Nivoda's fixed API addresses, to sign in for a 6-hour token.
howToGet: Use the API password Nivoda gives with the username.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: NIVODA_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Nivoda API to read: production or staging. Defaults to production; Nivoda gives staging access first and turns on production after testing.
howToGet: Set staging while testing with Nivoda's staging account.
Leave unset once Nivoda has turned on production.

entries.name: NIVODA_QUERY
entries.description: The saved search, as a JSON object in Nivoda's diamond query shape, such as shapes, sizes and lab-grown or natural. Every diamond Nivoda offers when unset, which NIVODA_MAX_STONES stops.
howToGet: Agree with the buyer which diamonds the business wants to watch.
Write them as Nivoda's query filter, and keep the search small enough to read: each 50 diamonds takes 30 seconds.

entries.name: NIVODA_MAX_STONES
entries.description: The most diamonds the search may find before the sync stops and asks for a narrower NIVODA_QUERY. Defaults to 1000; Nivoda pages up to 50000.
howToGet: Leave unset for 1000, about ten minutes of reading.
Raise it only for a search meant to cover more diamonds.

entries.name: NOTION_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: The secret of a Notion internal connection the connector reads data sources and pages with. Give the connection only the Read content capability, no user information, and share only the databases to sync with it. Notion's API can't report a connection's capabilities, so the connector can't check them; it only sends its own reads.
howToGet: Signed in to Notion as a workspace owner, open the integrations dashboard and create a new internal connection named KaratOS.
Under Capabilities, tick only Read content, and choose No user information.
In Notion, open each database to sync, choose Connections from its menu, and add KaratOS.
Copy the connection's secret straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: NOTION_DATA_SOURCE_IDS
entries.description: The ids of the Notion data sources to read, separated by commas. Unset reads every data source shared with the connection.
howToGet: Open the database in Notion, choose Manage data sources from its menu, and copy the data source's id.

entries.name: QUO_API_KEY
entries.description: An API key for the store's Quo (formerly OpenPhone) workspace, sent as the Authorization header. Quo keys have full access to the workspace's API, so the same key could send texts or change contacts; the connector only ever sends List calls and List messages. It goes only to Quo.
howToGet: A Quo workspace owner or admin opens Workspace Settings > API and creates a key named for KaratOS alone, so it can be deleted on its own.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: PINTEREST_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The App id of a Pinterest developer app the store owns. Not a secret on its own.
howToGet: Sign in to developers.pinterest.com as the store's Pinterest business account and open My apps.
Create an app (Pinterest reviews it before it can read a real account) and copy its App id.

entries.name: PINTEREST_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The same app's App secret key. It goes only to Pinterest's token endpoint, in a Basic header, and keys the encryption of the stored refresh token.
howToGet: In the app's page under My apps, show and copy the App secret key.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: PINTEREST_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the store's Pinterest business account connecting to the app with only boards:read, pins:read and user_accounts:read. The connector stops if the token holds any other scope. Pinterest replaces it on every refresh; the newest is kept, encrypted, in the instance's database, and it lapses after 60 days without a sync.
howToGet: In the app's page, generate a token with only boards:read, pins:read and user_accounts:read ticked, signed in as the store's business account.
If the account is a personal one, convert it to a free business account first; analytics need one.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: PIRO_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder of PIRO job and casting tree reports exported as CSV. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
In PIRO, export the job report and the casting tree report as CSV, with job or casting in the file name.
Save each export into the folder, or schedule PIRO's data extract to write there.

entries.name: PIRO_MAPPING_PROFILE
entries.description: Which columns this PIRO account's reports use: generic, or the path to a profile JSON file in the client's private instance repo.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the reports use PIRO's usual column names, such as Job No, Status, Tree No, Cast Date and Issued Weight (g).
Otherwise write a profile in the client's private instance repo and put the file's path here.

entries.name: PLAID_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS team on the Plaid Dashboard. It is the same in sandbox and production; the secret decides which.
howToGet: On dashboard.plaid.com, open Developers > Keys.
Copy the client_id straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: PLAID_SECRET
entries.description: The Plaid secret for the environment in PLAID_ENVIRONMENT: the Sandbox secret for sandbox, the Production secret for production. It is sent in the PLAID-SECRET header, never in a request body.
howToGet: On dashboard.plaid.com, open Developers > Keys and copy the secret for the environment the instance uses straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it on the Dashboard, update this value before the old secret is deleted.

entries.name: PLAID_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: The access token of the business's linked bank (a Plaid Item). It does not expire, and it reads that bank's accounts and transactions, so keep it as carefully as the bank login.
howToGet: Have the business link its bank through Plaid Link with the transactions product only, then exchange the public token Link returns with /item/public_token/exchange.
Copy the access token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
If a sync fails with ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED, have the business sign in again through Link's update mode; the token stays the same.

entries.name: PLAID_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Plaid API the Item is on: sandbox for Plaid's test banks, production for a real one. There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a client's bank by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use sandbox with the Sandbox secret and production with the Production secret.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS app on the Intuit Developer portal, used with the client secret to refresh QuickBooks access tokens.
howToGet: On developer.intuit.com, open the app under My Hub > App dashboard, then Keys and credentials. Use the Development keys with the sandbox company and the Production keys with the client's company.
Copy the Client ID straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the Intuit app. It refreshes access tokens and is the key the instance encrypts its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting QuickBooks.
howToGet: In the same Keys and credentials page, copy the Client Secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the company and set a new QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID
entries.description: The QuickBooks company's realm ID, shown as Company ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's books.
howToGet: The realmId comes back with the authorization code when the company is connected.
In QuickBooks it is under Settings > Account and settings > Billing and subscription, as Company ID.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the company. Intuit rotates it about daily, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have a QuickBooks admin connect the company to the KaratOS app with the com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting scope, for example through Intuit's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the app's own keys.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Intuit has no read-only accounting scope; the connector only sends GET requests, and its writes stay behind the write gate.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which QuickBooks API the company is on: sandbox for an Intuit developer sandbox company, production for a real one. There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a client's books by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use sandbox with Development keys and production with Production keys.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_WEBHOOK_VERIFIER_TOKEN
entries.description: Verifier token for QuickBooks webhooks, which signs each delivery (intuit-signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the app's Webhooks page on developer.intuit.com, copy the Verifier Token straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: RAMP_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client ID of a Ramp developer app made for KaratOS. It goes only to Ramp.
howToGet: In Ramp, open Company > Developer, create an app named KaratOS, add the client credentials grant type, and give it the transactions:read scope only, with no write scope.
Copy the client ID straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: RAMP_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The client secret of the same Ramp app. With the client ID it gets a token that can read card transactions only; the connector turns down a token granted any other scope. It goes only to Ramp.
howToGet: Ramp shows the secret when the app is created. Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: RAMP_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Optional. production for the business's Ramp account, or sandbox for a Ramp sandbox. Defaults to production.
howToGet: Leave it unset for the business's own Ramp account.

entries.name: RAPNET_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client ID of a Rapaport Trade API access key made for KaratOS. It names the key and isn't secret on its own.
howToGet: The primary account holder signs in to Rapaport Trade and opens Settings, Privacy, API Access.
Create an access key for KaratOS with the price list, and copy its client ID.

entries.name: RAPNET_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The client secret of that access key. KaratOS sends it only to Rapaport's token service, and uses the token to read the price list.
howToGet: Copy the client secret shown when the access key is created.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: REFINER_STATEMENTS_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder of refiner and scrap settlement statements, with one subfolder per refiner named in lowercase, such as test_refinery. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Inside it, make one folder per refiner, named in lowercase letters, digits and underscores.
Save each settlement statement the refiner sends, as CSV or PDF, into its folder.

entries.name: REFINER_STATEMENTS_PROFILES
entries.description: Which columns each refiner's statements use: generic, or the path to a JSON file in the client's private instance repo mapping refiner folders to parsing profiles.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the statements have Lot, Metal, Settlement Date and fine weight (or weight and assay) columns.
Otherwise write the profiles in the client's private instance repo and put the file's path here. PDF statements need a profile with a PDF layout.

entries.name: REPAIRSHOPR_API_TOKEN
entries.description: A RepairShopr API token made for KaratOS with custom permissions: only Tickets - List/Search, Estimates - List/Search and Invoices - List/Search. It goes only to the shop's RepairShopr account.
howToGet: Signed in to RepairShopr as an admin, open Admin > API > API Tokens and choose New Token. Name it KaratOS and choose Custom Permissions.
Tick only Tickets - List/Search, Estimates - List/Search and Invoices - List/Search, and leave every create, edit and delete permission unticked.
RepairShopr shows the token once. Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: REPAIRSHOPR_SUBDOMAIN
entries.description: The shop's RepairShopr subdomain: example in example.repairshopr.com.
howToGet: Copy it from the browser's address bar while signed in to RepairShopr.

entries.name: RFID_COUNTS_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder the RFID reader or barcode scanner software saves its tray count exports into, as CSV with one row per tag. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
In the reader or scanner software, export each count (or set it to export after each count) as CSV into that folder.
Check the export has a tray or case column, a tag or barcode column and a scan time column; docs/integrations/rfid_counts.md lists the names it reads.

entries.name: RFID_COUNTS_DATE_ORDER
entries.description: How the export writes dates: mdy (11/09/2026), dmy (09/11/2026) or ymd (2026-11-09).
howToGet: Leave unset for US dates, month first.

entries.name: RFID_COUNTS_UTC_OFFSET
entries.description: The store's offset from UTC, for scan times written without one, such as -05:00.
howToGet: Leave unset when the export writes times in UTC or with their own offset.

entries.name: RINGCENTRAL_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client id of the store's private KaratOS app in the RingCentral Developer Console, made for the JWT auth flow with only the ReadCallLog and ReadMessages permissions.
howToGet: In the RingCentral Developer Console, signed in as the store's RingCentral admin, create a REST API app named KaratOS, private to the store's account, with JWT auth flow as its only grant.
Under Application Scopes pick Read Call Log and Read Messages and nothing else. KaratOS stops if the app can do more.
Copy the Client ID from the app's Credentials.

entries.name: RINGCENTRAL_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The KaratOS app's client secret, sent only to RingCentral's sign-in as Basic auth, with the JWT, for a one-hour token.
howToGet: Copy the Client Secret from the KaratOS app's Credentials straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: RINGCENTRAL_JWT
entries.description: A JWT credential made by the RingCentral user whose extension is the store's line, allowed only for the KaratOS app. KaratOS reads that extension's calls, texts and voicemail, and no one else's.
howToGet: Signed in to the Developer Console as the user whose extension is the store's line, open Credentials and create a JWT named KaratOS.
Allow it for the KaratOS app's client id only, and give it the shortest expiry the store is happy to renew.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: STWM_API_KEY
entries.description: The Search The Watch Market Business API key, sent as a Bearer token to read prices, days to sell and price history. It goes only to Search The Watch Market.
howToGet: The store subscribes to a Business API plan on searchthewatchmarket.com. Once approved, the key appears under API Access in the account, as the vendor's API reference describes.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: STWM_REFERENCES
entries.description: The watch references or model names the store follows, comma or newline separated, up to 200.
howToGet: List the references the store buys, sells or takes in trade most often. A manufacturer reference number matches more reliably than a name.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_SHOP_DOMAIN
entries.description: The store's myshopify.com domain.
howToGet: In Shopify admin, go to Settings > Domains and copy the myshopify.com domain.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the store's Dev Dashboard app. With SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET, the connector requests a 24-hour Admin API token and renews it itself.
howToGet: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard as the store owner, so the app and the store share an organization.

Create an app, and in its version grant only these Admin API scopes: read_orders, read_all_orders, read_products, read_customers and read_inventory. Without read_all_orders Shopify returns only the last 60 days of orders. No write scopes.
Release the version, install the app on the store, then copy the Client ID from the app's Settings.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the store's Dev Dashboard app, used only to request Admin API tokens. It also signs webhooks, so set SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the same value.
howToGet: In the Shopify Dev Dashboard, open the app's Settings and copy the Client secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Permanent Admin API token of an older custom app made in the store admin. Use it instead of SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID and SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET only when the store already has such an app.
howToGet: Shopify stopped letting merchants create these apps on 2026-01-01; new stores use SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID and SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET.

For an existing app, in Shopify admin go to Settings > Apps and sales channels > Develop apps, check it holds only read_orders, read_all_orders, read_products, read_customers and read_inventory, and copy its Admin API access token.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_API_VERSION
entries.description: Shopify Admin API version the connector pins, e.g. 2026-07. Defaults to the version the connector was tested with.
howToGet: Leave empty to use the tested default. Shopify supports each quarterly version for 12 months; move up when the vendor docs watch reports a change.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The Shopify app's client secret, which signs webhook deliveries (X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256). Only needed when webhooks are turned on.
howToGet: For a Dev Dashboard app, use the same value as SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET.
For an older admin-made app, open its API credentials under Settings > Apps and sales channels > Develop apps and copy the API secret key.

entries.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
entries.description: The Bot User OAuth Token of the business's own Slack app, installed with read scopes only. The connector reads messages and threads in the channels the bot is invited to, and stops if the token holds any other scope, such as chat:write.
howToGet: At api.slack.com/apps, create a new app from scratch in the business's own workspace and don't distribute it, so it keeps Slack's internal-app limits.

Under OAuth & Permissions > Bot Token Scopes, add exactly channels:read and channels:history, and groups:read and groups:history if private channels should be read. Add nothing else: no chat:write, users:read or files:read.
Install the app to the workspace, copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-) straight into the host's secret store, then invite the bot (/invite @app-name) to each channel it should read.

entries.name: SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.description: Verifies Events API deliveries Slack sends to this instance (X-Slack-Signature). Optional: the instance doesn't take Slack webhooks yet, and the scheduled sync reads the same messages.
howToGet: At api.slack.com/apps, open the app > Basic Information > App Credentials, and copy the Signing Secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SLACK_TEXT_CHANNELS
entries.description: Which channels keep their message text: none (the default) keeps who posted, when and where but no text; all keeps text from every channel the bot is in; or a comma-separated list of channel ids. Kept text has email addresses, phone numbers, other numbers of seven or more digits, link paths and people's names taken out.
howToGet: Leave empty for none. To keep text, open each channel in Slack, click its name and copy the Channel ID at the bottom of the About tab, then list the ids separated by commas.

entries.name: SLACK_APP_DISTRIBUTION
entries.description: How the Slack app is distributed, which sets how fast history can be read: internal (the default), an app made in the business's own workspace, may read about 50 pages a minute; non_marketplace, an app installed from outside that isn't in the Slack Marketplace, may read 1 page of 15 messages a minute since May 2025.
howToGet: Leave empty for internal. Set non_marketplace only if the app was installed from another workspace and isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace.

entries.name: SMILE_API_KEY
entries.description: A Smile.io merchant API key made with only customer:read, points_transaction:read and vip_tier:read, so it can't change a balance. Merchant keys need Smile's Plus or Enterprise plan.
howToGet: In the Smile admin, the store owner makes an API key and gives it only the scopes customer:read, points_transaction:read and vip_tier:read. No write scope.
Copy the key, which starts with api_, straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
To revoke it, delete the key in the Smile admin.

entries.name: SOLA_API_KEY
entries.description: A Sola Payments API key for the account's transaction reports. Sola can't limit a key to reports, so it could also run sales and refunds; the connector only ever posts Report:All to Sola's reporting address. It goes only to Sola.
howToGet: In the Sola Portal, open Settings > Keys (Key Management), create an API key described as KaratOS reports, and give it the fewest permissions the portal allows.
Sola shows the key only once. Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: SOLA_TIME_ZONE
entries.description: Optional. The IANA time zone Sola's report times are in for this account. Defaults to America/New_York.
howToGet: Use the time zone the account's transactions show in on the Sola Portal's reports.

entries.name: SQUARE_APPLICATION_ID
entries.description: Application ID of the KaratOS app in the Square Developer Console. With SQUARE_APPLICATION_SECRET and SQUARE_REFRESH_TOKEN, the connector refreshes its access token and asks for the read scopes only each time. Not a secret.
howToGet: Sign in to developer.squareup.com, open the app (or create one for KaratOS), and copy the Application ID from its Credentials page. Use the Sandbox tab for testing and Production for the store.

entries.name: SQUARE_APPLICATION_SECRET
entries.description: The Square app's application secret, used only to refresh the OAuth access token.
howToGet: On the app's OAuth page in the Square Developer Console, show the Application secret and copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SQUARE_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the seller authorizing the KaratOS app (the OAuth code flow). Square keeps returning the same one, so it doesn't need saving after each refresh; revoking the app's access ends it.
howToGet: Have the seller authorize the app with exactly these scopes: MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ ITEMS_READ INVENTORY_READ CUSTOMERS_READ ORDERS_READ PAYMENTS_READ. No _WRITE scopes: the connector stops if the token holds any other scope.
Exchange the authorization code for tokens (ObtainToken with grant_type authorization_code) and copy the refresh_token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Instead of the three OAuth settings above: an OAuth access token already limited to the read scopes. It lasts 30 days and is not refreshed. A personal access token from the Developer Console has full access, so the connector stops with one.
howToGet: Prefer SQUARE_APPLICATION_ID, SQUARE_APPLICATION_SECRET and SQUARE_REFRESH_TOKEN. Use this only for a short test with an OAuth token holding exactly MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ ITEMS_READ INVENTORY_READ CUSTOMERS_READ ORDERS_READ PAYMENTS_READ.

entries.name: SQUARE_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Square host to read: production (connect.squareup.com) or sandbox (connect.squareupsandbox.com). production when empty.
howToGet: Leave empty for a live store. Set sandbox only for a Square developer sandbox seller.

entries.name: SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY
entries.description: Signature key of the app's webhook subscription, which signs each delivery (x-square-hmacsha256-signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In the Square Developer Console, open the app's Webhooks > Subscriptions, pick the subscription and copy its Signature key straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SQUARE_WEBHOOK_URL
entries.description: The notification URL set on the webhook subscription, character for character. Square signs it together with the body, so a different URL fails every check.
howToGet: Copy the Notification URL from the same webhook subscription in the Square Developer Console.

entries.name: SQUARESPACE_API_KEY
entries.description: A Squarespace Commerce API key made with Read Only permission for Orders, Inventory and Products, and no permission for anything else. Custom API keys need the Commerce Advanced plan. The key doesn't expire while the site is active.
howToGet: Signed in to the site as an admin, open Settings, Advanced, Developer API Keys and click Generate Key.
Name it KaratOS, tick Orders, Inventory and Products, and set each to Read Only. Leave every other API unticked.
Squarespace shows the key once: copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
To cut KaratOS off, revoke the key on the same page.

entries.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
entries.description: Restricted Stripe key with read-only access. A full secret key (sk_) is rejected, because it can move money.
howToGet: In the Stripe dashboard, go to Developers > API keys and select Create restricted key.
Set Read on charges, refunds, disputes, payouts, balance and balance transactions, customers and events. Leave every other permission at None.
Copy the key, which starts rk_live_, straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Verifies that webhooks really came from Stripe.
howToGet: In Stripe, go to Developers > Webhooks, add this instance's webhook URL with the charge, refund, dispute, payout and customer events, and copy its signing secret.

entries.name: STRIPE_API_VERSION
entries.description: Stripe API version the connector pins, e.g. 2026-09-30.endive. Defaults to the version the connector was tested with.
howToGet: Leave empty to use the tested default. Move up when the vendor docs watch reports a Stripe changelog change that the connector has been tested against.

entries.name: STULLER_USERNAME
entries.description: The username of a Stuller developer login made for KaratOS. A developer login works only for the API and can't sign in to Stuller.com.
howToGet: The Stuller.com account owner, or a user with the Administrator role, signs in and adds a user with the Developer role for KaratOS.
Copy that login's username.

entries.name: STULLER_PASSWORD
entries.description: The password of that developer login. KaratOS sends it only to api.stuller.com, over https.
howToGet: Set it when creating the developer login.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: SUPPLIER_INVOICES_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder of supplier invoice and memo exports, with one subfolder per supplier named in lowercase, such as test_supplier. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Inside it, make one folder per supplier, named in lowercase letters, digits and underscores.
Save each invoice and memo export the supplier sends, or the accounting system writes, as CSV into its folder.

entries.name: SUPPLIER_INVOICES_PROFILES
entries.description: Which columns each supplier's exports use: generic, or the path to a JSON file in the client's private instance repo mapping supplier folders to parsing profiles.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the exports have an invoice or memo number, a date, and an amount or unit price column.
Otherwise write the profiles in the client's private instance repo and put the file's path here.

entries.name: TAXJAR_API_TOKEN
entries.description: The business's TaxJar API token, sent as a Bearer token. TaxJar can't limit a token to reading, so it could record, change or delete transactions; the connector only ever sends its five GETs. It goes only to TaxJar.
howToGet: In TaxJar, an account owner opens Account, chooses TaxJar API on the left and selects Generate API Token. TaxJar gives tokens to Professional accounts; on another plan, ask TaxJar support about API access.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: TAXJAR_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Optional. Which TaxJar the token is for: production (api.taxjar.com) or sandbox (api.sandbox.taxjar.com). Production when left empty.
howToGet: Leave empty for the store's live account. Use sandbox with a token made for TaxJar's sandbox.

entries.name: TAXJAR_PROVIDERS
entries.description: Optional. Where the store's transactions were recorded in TaxJar, comma-separated, such as api,shopify. TaxJar lists one source at a time and only api, the ones sent through its API, when none is named.
howToGet: Leave empty when the store sends sales to TaxJar through its API. Otherwise name each source on the store's TaxJar Transactions page, such as shopify or amazon, and check the first sync reads them.

entries.name: TIKTOK_CLIENT_KEY
entries.description: The client key of a TikTok for Developers app the store owns, with Login Kit and the Display API added. Not a secret on its own.
howToGet: Sign in to developers.tiktok.com and open Manage apps, then create an app for the store.
Add Login Kit and the Display API, ask only for user.info.basic, user.info.stats and video.list, and submit the app for TikTok's review.
Copy the app's Client key.

entries.name: TIKTOK_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The same app's client secret. It goes only to TikTok's token endpoint, in the form body as TikTok's docs say, and keys the encryption of the stored refresh token.
howToGet: In the app's page under Manage apps, show and copy the Client secret.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: TIKTOK_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the store's TikTok account signing in to the app and allowing only user.info.basic, user.info.stats and video.list. The connector stops if the token holds any other scope. TikTok may replace it on a refresh; the newest is kept, encrypted, in the instance's database. It lasts a year from when the account signed in.
howToGet: Sign in to the app with the store's TikTok account and allow the three permissions it asks for, nothing more.
Copy the refresh token from the sign-in's answer straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Sign in again before the year is up and replace it.

entries.name: TIKTOK_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: A long-lived advertiser access token from a TikTok for Business developer app made with read scopes only: Ad Account Information (read) and Reporting. Never an app with Ads Management or any scope that can change a campaign. The token doesn't expire unless it is revoked.
howToGet: In the TikTok for Business Developers portal, create an app and tick only the read scopes Ad Account Information and Reporting, then submit it for review.
Once it is approved, open its advertiser authorization link signed in as someone with access to the store's ad account, and approve that account.
Exchange the auth code for a token at /open_api/v1.3/oauth2/access_token/ with the app's ID and secret.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: TIKTOK_ADS_ADVERTISER_ID
entries.description: The numeric ID of the advertiser (ad account) Brain A reads. Not a secret.
howToGet: In TikTok Ads Manager, the advertiser ID is under the account name at the top right, and in the token answer's advertiser_ids.

entries.name: TIKTOK_ADS_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Optional. production for the store's own ad account, or sandbox for a sandbox advertiser made in the developer portal. Defaults to production. Not a secret.
howToGet: Leave it unset for a real ad account. Set it to sandbox only for a sandbox advertiser.

entries.name: TRELLO_API_KEY
entries.description: The API key of a Trello Power-Up made for KaratOS. On its own it reads nothing, but it is kept with the token.
howToGet: Signed in to Trello as the client's admin, open the Power-Up admin portal (trello.com/power-ups/admin), create a Power-Up named KaratOS in the client's workspace, and open its API key tab.
Generate a new API key and copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: TRELLO_TOKEN
entries.description: A Trello token authorized with scope=read only, for the member whose boards are read. The connector asks Trello what the token may do before every sync and stops if it can write.
howToGet: As a member who can see the boards to sync and no more, open https://trello.com/1/authorize?expiration=never&scope=read&response_type=token&name=KaratOS&key= followed by TRELLO_API_KEY.
Check the page says KaratOS will be able to read, and nothing more, then allow it.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: TRUSTPILOT_API_KEY
entries.description: The API key of a Trustpilot application, for reading the store's public reviews and trust score. Only the key: the application's API secret is never asked for, so KaratOS can't reply to reviews or send invitations. It goes only to Trustpilot.
howToGet: The store needs Trustpilot's API module. Create an API application as Trustpilot's help article on using its APIs describes (linked from its Authentication overview).
Copy only the API key. Leave the API secret in Trustpilot.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: TRUSTPILOT_BUSINESS_UNIT_ID
entries.description: The store's Trustpilot business unit id: 24 characters from 0-9 and a-f.
howToGet: Look it up once with Trustpilot's Find a business unit call, giving the API key and the store's domain, as Trustpilot's Business Units API overview shows.

entries.name: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID
entries.description: The Twilio account whose message and call logs are read.
howToGet: Shown on the Twilio Console home page as Account SID (AC followed by 32 characters).

entries.name: TWILIO_API_KEY_SID
entries.description: SID of a restricted API key that can only read message and call logs. The account's Auth Token is never used: it can change anything on the account.
howToGet: In the Twilio Console, go to Account > API keys & tokens and create a Restricted key named KaratOS read-only.
Give it only the read permissions for Messaging messages and Voice calls, and no others.
Copy the key's SID (SK followed by 32 characters).

entries.name: TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET
entries.description: Secret of the restricted API key.
howToGet: Shown once, when the restricted key is created. Put it straight into the password manager and the instance settings.

entries.name: TWILIO_CONTACT_KEY
entries.description: The instance's own key for turning customers' phone numbers into contact references (HMAC-SHA256), so texts and calls with the same person line up without the number being kept. Changing it gives every customer a new reference, so it is never rotated.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Keep a copy in the password manager.

entries.name: UPS_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The Client ID of a UPS developer app with the Tracking product. It is sent to UPS only, with the secret, to sign in.
howToGet: Sign in at developer.ups.com with the business's UPS account and open Apps.
Add an app for KaratOS, link the shipper account, add only the Tracking product, and copy its Client ID.

entries.name: UPS_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The app's Client Secret. With only the Tracking product added, it can read tracking and nothing else: no labels, pickups or billing.
howToGet: On the same app's page at developer.ups.com, copy the Client Secret.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: UPS_TRACKING_NUMBERS_FILE
entries.description: A text or CSV file of the UPS tracking numbers to follow, one or more a line, such as the labels printed for repairs, memo goods and customer orders. Lines starting with # are skipped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Export the tracking numbers from UPS's shipping history, the POS or the shipping app.
Save it outside any git repo and put its path here. Add new numbers as parcels go out; delivered ones are no longer read.

entries.name: UPS_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: production (the default) reads live tracking; test uses UPS's Customer Integration Environment, which only answers UPS's test numbers.
howToGet: Leave unset for live tracking.

entries.name: UPS_MAX_TRACKING_PER_SYNC
entries.description: The most tracking numbers one sync reads, oldest first. Defaults to 500, so a long list can't use up the app's daily call limit in one sync.
howToGet: Leave unset for 500.

entries.name: VERKADA_API_KEY
entries.description: A read-only Verkada API key from the organization's admin, for reading occupancy trends. It is traded for a 30-minute token and goes only to Verkada.
howToGet: An organization admin opens the Verkada API tab under Organization Settings in Command, chooses + New API Key, picks Read-only permissions and an expiration, and generates the key, as Verkada's quick start guide describes. Permissions can't be changed later, so choose Read-only when making it.
The key is shown once. Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: VERKADA_REGION
entries.description: Where the organization's Verkada data lives: us (the default) or eu.
howToGet: Leave it unset for the US address, api.verkada.com. Set it to eu for an organization on api.eu.verkada.com, as Verkada's quick start guide lists.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder where WhatsApp chat exports from the store's dealer groups are saved, one .txt file per group, named after the group. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.

In WhatsApp, open each dealer group, choose Export chat > Without media, and save the .txt file into the folder named after the group, such as Rolex Dealers HK.txt. On iPhone the export is a zip holding _chat.txt: unzip it and rename the file.
Export again whenever you want fresh offers; a newer export of the same group replaces the old file, and offers already read are recognized.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_DEALER_KEY
entries.description: The instance's own key for turning dealer names and numbers into dealer references (HMAC-SHA256), so offers from the same dealer line up without the name or number being kept. Changing it gives every dealer a new reference, so it is never rotated.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Keep a copy in the password manager: losing it means earlier offers no longer line up with new ones by dealer.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_DATE_ORDER
entries.description: How the phone that exports the chats writes dates: auto, dmy (22/10/2026) or mdy (10/22/2026). Auto works it out from each file.
howToGet: Leave as auto. Set dmy or mdy only when a sync says a file's dates could be read either way, which happens when every message in it is from the first 12 days of a month.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_UTC_OFFSET
entries.description: The exporting phone's offset from UTC, such as +08:00 or -05:00. Exports carry the phone's local times.
howToGet: Use the time zone of the phone that exports the chats. Leave it empty for UTC.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_CURRENCY
entries.description: The currency the store's groups mean when a dealer writes a bare price such as 14.5k. Without it, those prices are left out and only prices with a currency are kept.
howToGet: Set it when most of the store's groups trade in one currency, using its three-letter code (USD, EUR, HKD).

entries.name: WIX_APP_ID
entries.description: The App ID of the self-managed Wix app KaratOS reads the site through. An app, not an API key: Wix lets the connector read back an app's granted permissions, so it can stop if any Manage permission is present, and only apps receive webhooks.
howToGet: In the Wix app dashboard (manage.wix.com, Custom Apps), open the KaratOS app and go to Develop > OAuth.
Copy the App ID.

entries.name: WIX_APP_SECRET
entries.description: The app's secret key, used only to request four-hour access tokens for the site (OAuth client credentials). The app must hold read permissions only; the connector stops on any Manage or write permission.
howToGet: In the app's dashboard, go to Develop > OAuth and copy the App Secret Key straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: WIX_INSTANCE_ID
entries.description: The app's instance ID on the client's site: one per site the app is installed on. It names the site in each token request and keys the site's customer references.
howToGet: Install the app on the client's site; the site owner approves its read permissions.
Wix sends the instance ID with the app's App Instance Installed webhook; copy it from there, or from the app's installation details in its dashboard.

entries.name: WIX_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY
entries.description: The app's public key (PEM), which verifies each webhook: Wix signs every delivery as a JWT (RS256). Not secret. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it. An API key gets no webhooks.
howToGet: In the app's dashboard, go to Develop > Webhooks and choose Public Key.
Copy the whole key, from the BEGIN PUBLIC KEY line to the END PUBLIC KEY line.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_STORE_URL
entries.description: The WooCommerce store's home address, https only, e.g. https://shop.example.com (or https://example.com/shop when WordPress lives in a folder). Every request goes here and nowhere else: the connector refuses http, IP addresses, ports, user names in the address and hostnames that resolve to private networks, and never follows a redirect.
howToGet: Open the store in a browser and copy the address it settles on, including https:// and www. if the store uses it, without /wp-admin or /wp-json.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_KEY
entries.description: Consumer key of a WooCommerce REST API key with Read permission. WooCommerce has no way to ask a key's permission without sending a write, so the connector can't check it; it sends GET requests only, and a Read key keeps the store safe even if that ever failed.
howToGet: In WordPress, open WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API and choose Add key.
Describe it as KaratOS, pick an administrator or shop manager as the user, and set Permissions to Read. Never Write or Read/Write.
Generate the key and copy the Consumer key (it starts ck_) straight into the host's secret store. WooCommerce shows it only once.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_SECRET
entries.description: Consumer secret of the same Read key. Sent only in the Authorization header over https, never in an address.
howToGet: Copy the Consumer secret (it starts cs_) shown with the key straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The secret set on the store's webhooks, which signs each delivery (X-WC-Webhook-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Paste it as the Secret of each webhook under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Webhooks. Letters and digits only: WooCommerce decodes HTML entities in the secret before signing.

entries.name: XERO_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS app in Xero's developer portal, used with the client secret to refresh Xero access tokens.
howToGet: On developer.xero.com, open My Apps, pick the app (a Web app), then Configuration.
Copy the Client id straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: XERO_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the Xero app. It refreshes access tokens and is the key the instance encrypts its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting Xero.
howToGet: On the app's Configuration page, generate a client secret and copy it straight into the host's secret store. Xero shows it once.
After rotating it, reconnect the organisation and set a new XERO_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: XERO_TENANT_ID
entries.description: The Xero organisation's tenant ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's books.
howToGet: After the organisation is connected, call GET https://api.xero.com/connections with the access token and copy the tenantId of the organisation (tenantType ORGANISATION).
A connection can cover several organisations; each one needs its own instance.

entries.name: XERO_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the organisation. Xero retires it on every refresh and drops it after 60 days unused, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have a Xero adviser or standard user connect the organisation to the KaratOS app with exactly these scopes: offline_access accounting.settings.read accounting.contacts.read accounting.invoices.read accounting.payments.read accounting.banktransactions.read accounting.manualjournals.read.
The connector rejects a connection holding any scope beyond read-only, so don't add others.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: XERO_WEBHOOK_KEY
entries.description: Webhook signing key for Xero webhooks, which signs each delivery (x-xero-signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the app's Webhooks page on developer.xero.com, copy the Webhooks key straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: YEXT_API_KEY
entries.description: An API key of a Yext app the store owns. Give the app read access to Entities and Reviews and nothing else: Yext keys carry no scopes the connector could check, and it only ever sends GETs. It goes only to Yext, in an api-key header.
howToGet: In Yext, open Developer, then Developer Console, and add an app for KaratOS.
Under the app's API permissions, give Entities and Reviews read-only access and leave everything else off.
Copy the app's API key straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: YEXT_ACCOUNT_ID
entries.description: The Yext account to read. Leave it unset to read the account the key belongs to, which is what most stores want; set it only for a sub-account.
howToGet: Leave unset, or copy the account id from Yext's account settings.

entries.name: YEXT_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: production, or sandbox for a Yext sandbox account. production when unset.
howToGet: Leave unset unless the key belongs to a Yext sandbox account.

entries.name: YOTPO_STORE_ID
entries.description: The store's Yotpo store ID, also called the app key.
howToGet: In Yotpo, open the Reviews main menu, choose Settings > General Settings and copy the Store ID.

entries.name: YOTPO_API_SECRET
entries.description: The store's Yotpo API secret, which gets an access token for reading reviews. Yotpo can't limit it to reading, so it could also moderate and reply to reviews; the connector only ever asks for a token and lists reviews. It goes only to Yotpo.
howToGet: On the same General Settings page, an account admin selects Get API secret and confirms by email.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: YOTPO_LOYALTY_GUID
entries.description: Optional. The GUID of the store's Yotpo Loyalty program, to read members' points and tiers. Give it with YOTPO_LOYALTY_API_KEY, or leave both empty to read reviews only.
howToGet: In the Yotpo Loyalty app, open Settings and copy the GUID.

entries.name: YOTPO_LOYALTY_API_KEY
entries.description: Optional. The Loyalty program's API key, sent with the GUID. Yotpo can't limit it to reading, so it could also adjust points and create redemptions; the connector only lists recently updated members. It goes only to Yotpo.
howToGet: On the same Loyalty Settings page, copy the API key.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN
entries.description: The store's Zendesk subdomain: store for store.zendesk.com. Every request goes to that address.
howToGet: Read it from the address bar of the store's Zendesk: the part before .zendesk.com.

entries.name: ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The unique identifier of the OAuth client a Zendesk admin made for KaratOS in Admin Center.
howToGet: A Zendesk admin opens Admin Center, Apps and integrations, APIs, OAuth Clients, and adds a client named KaratOS (a confidential client).
Copy the client's unique identifier.

entries.name: ZENDESK_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The KaratOS OAuth client's secret, sent only to the store's Zendesk sign-in, with the refresh token, for a short-lived token. It also seals the rotated refresh token in the instance's database.
howToGet: Zendesk shows the secret once, when the OAuth client is saved. Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: ZENDESK_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from a Zendesk admin authorizing the KaratOS client for only tickets:read and users:read. Refresh tokens are single-use: KaratOS keeps the newest, encrypted, in its database, and this one seeds it. Each lasts 90 days, so a sync at least that often keeps it alive.
howToGet: A Zendesk admin authorizes the KaratOS client through Zendesk's authorization code flow, asking for the scopes tickets:read and users:read and nothing else. Incremental exports need an admin's token.
Exchange the code at POST /oauth/tokens and put the answer's refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
To revoke it, delete the token or the OAuth client in Admin Center.

entries.name: ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID
entries.description: The Account ID shown on the App Credentials page of the store's KaratOS app, a Server-to-Server OAuth app in the Zoom App Marketplace.
howToGet: A Zoom admin signs in to marketplace.zoom.us, chooses Develop > Build App, picks Server-to-Server OAuth App and names it KaratOS.
On the Scopes page, add only report:read:list_history_meetings:admin and report:read:list_meeting_participants:admin. Add nothing else: the connector won't read with a token that can change anything.
Activate the app, then copy the Account ID from App Credentials.

entries.name: ZOOM_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The Client ID of the same KaratOS app.
howToGet: Copy the Client ID from the KaratOS app's App Credentials page.

entries.name: ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The Client Secret of the KaratOS app. With the account and client ids it gets an hour-long token each sync, and it goes only to Zoom.
howToGet: Copy the Client Secret from the KaratOS app's App Credentials page.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
